subject.title: Telegram should default to allowlist mode with owner ID

question: Should Telegram first-run setup move to token-verified owner capture that writes dmPolicy="allowlist" and allowFrom by default, or should pairing remain the default with stronger warnings and manual allowlist setup?
rationale: This chooses the trust boundary for who can request access to a bundled private Telegram bot during first-run setup, and it affects compatibility for users who rely on pairing as the omitted-policy behavior.

options.title: Adopt verified owner capture
options.body: Fresh Telegram setup displays a short random token, captures only the sender who sends that token, and stores allowlist mode for that owner by default.

options.title: Keep pairing default
options.body: Current pairing remains the default while setup and docs more strongly route one-owner deployments to manual numeric allowlists.

options.title: Fold into broader bootstrap design
options.body: Keep this issue as context while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48471 or https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/81876 defines the permanent product contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt verified owner capture
recommendation.body: Fresh Telegram setup displays a short random token, captures only the sender who sends that token, and stores allowlist mode for that owner by default.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the prior detailed product/security review on this issue and is the clearest owner signal for the Telegram setup/default policy choice.
